Topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space

Target audience: High school or introductory university students

Section: section_1 — What is a Vector? (The Intuition)

Lecture lines:
Vectors have both magnitude and direction.
Scalars are just magnitude values.
Think of a drone's flight path.
We represent vectors as arrows.
Arrows show direction and length.

Planned animations:
Draw a Dot (#FFFFFF) representing a point in 2D space.
Draw an arrow (#FFFF00) from the origin to the Dot.
Animate the arrow transforming to indicate displacement.
Highlight the tip of the vector with a circle (#FF0000).
Show the label 'v' near the vector.

Section: section_2 — Coordinate Representation & Components

Lecture lines:
We use grids to map space.
Vectors break into horizontal components.
They also have vertical components.

Planned animations:
Draw a standard grid system (#808080).
Place a point at (3, 2) and draw vector 'v' from origin.
Animate dotted lines to (3, 0) and (0, 2) indicating components.
Label x-component '3' and y-component '2' (#00FF00).

Section: section_3 — Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule

Lecture lines:
Connect the head to the tail.
This adds two vectors together.
The result is a new vector.

Planned animations:
Draw vector 'u' starting at origin.
Translate vector 'v' to start at the tip of 'u'.
Draw a resultant vector 'u+v' from origin to tip of 'v'.

Section: section_4 — Scalar Multiplication & Scaling

Lecture lines:
Scalars stretch or shrink vectors.
Direction stays same if positive.
Negative scalars reverse the direction.

Planned animations:
Draw vector 'v' (#00FFFF).
Scale vector 'v' by 2, show length doubling.
Scale vector 'v' by -1, show direction reversal.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Vectors power modern data science.
Physics engines use them too.
They map our entire world.

Planned animations:
Show a 2D map overlay with displacement vectors.
Animate a particle following the path of combined vectors.
Display text 'Vectors define movement in space'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
